## Short answer

Lemonade beat — or landed at the very top of — the full-year 2024 guidance it issued with Q3 2024 results (Oct 30, 2024) on essentially every line. **In-force premium** came in at the high end of the range, **revenue and gross earned premium** came in modestly *above* the top of the ranges, and the **Adjusted EBITDA loss** was smaller than the guidance's best case. Management framed it as delivering its original February 2024 guidance "with notable precision."

## The comparison

| FY2024 metric | Q3'24 guidance (issued Oct 30, 2024) | FY2024 actual (reported Feb 26, 2025) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| In-force premium (IFP) | $940–$944M | **$943.7M** (+26% YoY) | ✅ High end of range |
| Gross earned premium | $823–$826M | **$827.3M** (+23%) | ✅ ~$1.3M above high end |
| Revenue | $522–$524M | **$526.5M** (+22.5%) | ✅ ~$2.5M above high end |
| Adjusted EBITDA loss | ($155)–($151)M | **($149.7)M** | ✅ ~$1.3M better than best case |
| Stock-based comp | ~$64M | **$64.5M** | ≈ In line |
| Capital expenditures | ~$10M | **~$8M** (derived from cash flow stmt.) | ≈ At/below plan |
| Weighted avg. shares | ~71M | **71.0M** | ≈ In line |

Not guided, but reported: **net loss** narrowed ~15% to ($202.2)M (vs. ($236.9)M in 2023), **gross profit** nearly doubled to $166.9M (+98%), TTM **gross loss ratio** hit 73% — inside the long-term target range and 12 points better YoY — and the company generated its **first full year of positive Adjusted Free Cash Flow: +$48M**.

## Why the year beat: the Q4 overperformance

Q4 itself beat on every guided line, which is what pushed the full year past the top end:

| Q4 2024 | Guidance | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| IFP | $940–$944M | $943.7M |
| Gross earned premium | $222–$225M | $226.4M |
| Revenue | $144–$146M | $148.8M |
| Adjusted EBITDA loss | ($29)–($25)M | ($23.8)M |

Q4 gross loss ratio of 63% was a company record, gross profit rose 90% to $63.9M, and Adj. FCF was +$26.5M. Notably, Q4 was also the first quarter ever with **positive Adj. EBITDA excluding growth spend**.

## Context worth flagging

- **Guidance had already been raised mid-year.** The Q3 update raised FY2024 GEP and revenue guidance while reaffirming IFP and Adj. EBITDA. Against the *original* February 2024 guide (IFP $938–$942M; Adj. EBITDA loss ($160)–($155)M), the beat looks larger: IFP of $944M and a ($150)M EBITDA loss.
- **The beat was achieved despite headwinds** — elevated inflation and one of the most active catastrophe seasons in recent memory — and despite ~$25M of homeowners' IFP deliberately non-renewed in H2 2024 to reduce CAT volatility.
- **The cost line did the heavy lifting.** Growth spend more than doubled ($55M → $122M), yet total expenses *excluding* growth spend grew only 2% ($332M) against 26% IFP growth — that operating leverage is what drove the EBITDA beat and the swing to positive cash flow.

⚠️ One caveat: some secondary coverage of this quarter (e.g., certain syndicated articles) misreported the FY2024 capex and SBC figures — capex ~$60M and SBC ~$10M — which appear to be transposed. The shareholder letter and 10-K show SBC of $64.5M and capex in the single-digit millions.
